# Ra.One
**Ra.One** is a 2011 Indian science fiction action film directed by Anubhav Sinha, starring Shah Rukh Khan in a dual role as the programmer Shekhar Subramaniam and his superhero avatar, G. One. The story follows Shekhar, who creates a video game with his son Prateek where the villain, Ra.One, possesses superior abilities including shapeshifting and a self-learning AI. When the game launches, Ra.One breaks free from the digital world into the real world, leading to the deaths of Shekhar and his colleague Akashi. G. One and Prateek then attempt to bring the hero to life, but Ra.One hunts them across India, eventually kidnapping Prateek and causing chaos before G. One and Prateek defeat the villain in a climactic battle.
The film's production was marked by significant challenges, including a massive budget, extensive visual effects work involving over 1,200 artists, and the creation of custom superhero suits for Khan and Arjun Rampal. It faced controversies regarding cultural representation in its dialogue and plagiarism allegations comparing its concept to other sci-fi franchises. Upon release, the film became the widest-released Hindi film at the time, setting pre-sale and opening weekend records, though it received mixed critical reviews domestically. It was later remastered and re-released in 3D, cementing its legacy as a high-profile attempt at a superhero franchise in Bollywood.
